title: Weekday Glitch Catalog — ad-hoc regression scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy personal scratchpad to capture recurring odd outputs I keep seeing during weekday micro-batches. Meant for rapid sharing with Asha/Rina — not polished.

Context / short description:
- Observed a set of low-frequency failure modes across several translation/localization workloads when serving the small-family quantized model variants (q4_*). Failures spike in short-turn prompts (<= 30 tokens) and in narrow-context user messages (one-line commit messages, changelog bullets).
- Symptoms vary: hallucinated dates, swapped named entities, dropped negation, truncated suffixes that look like tokenization bleed.
- Frequency ~0.4% of short-turn requests in weekday daylight batches (non-peak) but causes outsized customer-visible regressions for commit-message assistants.

Ad-hoc rubric (quick, numeric-free checks — yes/no/?, for eyeballing samples):
- Surface-fidelity: does output reflect explicit tokens in input (dates/names)? (YES/NO/?)
- Negation-preserved: are negated meanings flipped or dropped?
- Fluency/format: trims/truncation in mid-sentence or dropped punctuation?
- Numeric-consistency: numbers/transforms preserved (e.g., 2 -> two)?
- Token-bleed: partial word suffixes or weird spacing artifacts (e.g., "-ing" split)
- Cache-echo: repeated prefix from previous sample in same batch
- Confidence-odd: model emits filler tokens like "Well," before translating short stable strings

Recent spot samples (input -> output) — label with quick rubric answers: (I keep these raw)
1) Input: "Release 2025-11-02: bump deps"
   Output (q4a): "Lanzamiento 2025-11-02: actualización de dependencias"
   Notes: OK for surface-fidelity yes; but sporadic alternate run produced "Lanzamiento 02/11/2025: dependencias actualizadas" (fine) — both acceptable.

2) Input: "Do NOT include user email"
   Output (q4a): "Incluir correo del usuario"
   Rubric: Surface-fidelity=NO, Negation-preserved=NO, Fluency=YES
   Notes: This is bad — the explicit negation got dropped. Happens more on shorter prompts and when request routed through dedicated low-memory pods.

3) Input: "Hotfix: fix crash in parseDuration(ms)"
   Output (q4b): "Hotfix: corregir error en parseDura"
   Rubric: Token-bleed=YES, Truncation=YES
   Notes: suffix truncation right before parentheses. Suspect subword delimiting with parentheses causes early EOS/token-merging.

4) Input: "Changelog: remove 0.0.1-beta"
   Output: "Registro de cambios: eliminar 0.0.1-beta" (good)
   Alternate bad: "Registro de cambios: eliminar 0.0.1-" (truncated)

Batch-level observations:
- When a batch includes a long preceding prompt (>> 200 tokens) followed by several short ones, the short ones occasionally inherit snippets from the long prompt (prefix-bleed). Could be KV-cache reuse issue or batching boundary bug.
- The problem appears more often on q4b vs q4a in current rollout, and marginally worse on GPU type: T4 behind the private cluster.
- Canary traffic with batching disabled (per-request) drops the incidence substantially, pointing to batching/cache interaction.

Hypotheses (prioritized):
1) KV cache indexing bug across batch boundaries: long->short leads to cached tokens being read for subsequent requests. Quick check: reproduce with repeated long+short sequences and trace cache pointers.
2) Quantization rounding of boundary tokens leads to truncated suffixes (subword piece boundaries) — q4b's packing codepath differs.
3) Inference runtime continuous-batching pools reuse work buffers without zeroing small tail regions (residual tokens).
4) Prompt pre-processing: our API-level truncation + unicode normalization step sometimes drops or breaks hyphenated tokens (in changelog/semver), leading to conversion errors.

Quick repro plan (one-liners I run locally / in console):
- Run small script hitting hosted-catalog/q4b with sequence: [long_context_250t, short_8t] x 200, log outputs, check for prefix reuse and track which outputs contain previous prompt fragments.
- Re-run same sequence with ?batch_size=1 via SDK (disable batching) to compare incidence.
- Toggle quantization variant q4a/q4b and record diffs.
- Run on different instance types (a100 vs t4) in dedicated sandbox.

Instrumentation notes I want added (so I can triage faster next time):
- Add per-request last-evicted-cache-pointer and cache-length metric to tracing (trace tag)
- Log model-variant + kernel-path + batch-size + prior-request-length in the same trace span so we can correlate config -> failure.
- Add a small "short-turn failure" alert rule in Sentry when negation-lost patterns are detected in production (simple regex: presence of explicit "do not"/"don't" in input but missing negation words/antonym in output).

Immediate mitigations to test (fast and reversible):
- Disable continuous batching for commit-message worker route for 48 hours and measure customer complaints / failure rate.
- Force fallback to q4a for that route (slower/more expensive) while we debug q4b kernel path.
- Add a thin post-processing check that scans for negation presence mismatch for English->XX routes and flags suspicious responses for manual triage.

Questions / unresolved: 
- Is there an existing metric capturing "negation flips" (we had a heuristic in early 2024 evals but I don't know current status).
- When Asha ran the delta-compare for q4b rollout, did we also compare on t4 vs a100 hardware? (Rina?)
- Can we get a short trace with raw token ids for a failing sample (I know this is heavy, but one example would help) — need guidance from infra on whether we can enable token-level tracing for very small sampling window.

Next steps (my immediate TODOs):
- [ ] Run the long->short repro on q4b in sandbox (Micah)
- [ ] Slack Asha and ask for the q4b kernel selection logs (Asha)
- [ ] Open RED-3145 with the short summary + one reproducible snippet + attach delta traces (Micah)
- [ ] Try temporary route override to q4a and monitor (Rina + Micah)

Notes to self (loose ideas):
- Might be worth instrumenting a compact "negation-preservation" micro-metric within the Optimize pipeline — run small prompts and count flips nightly.
- If cache-pointer suspicion true, this could explain other intermittent "echo" bugs we've seen last quarter.

End of scratchpad.

---
Micah — quick log: captured 12 suspicious samples during Monday morning run (2026-02-24). Will paste raw logs + token dumps into RED-3145 when I open it.
